category_title: Integrated student with ADHD who uses self-regulation and support staff to manage sensory/social overwhelm
student_description: Adam is a student with ADHD who experiences severe sensory overwhelm in noisy, unstructured environments, leading him to withdraw (e.g., hiding under tables, reading by windowsills) to prevent angry outbursts. He uniquely requires adults to accept his temporary withdrawal as a valid self-regulation strategy, alongside targeted pedagogue support to manage environmental noise and proactively plan for known difficult lessons.

criteria.rationale: Unstructured group organization overwhelms Adam, whereas structured cooperative learning safely promotes his social interaction and integration.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate structured cooperative learning frameworks rather than relying on chaotic, self-organized group work.

criteria.rationale: Collaborating with Adam to identify his hardest moments allows for targeted pedagogue support before sensory overwhelm occurs.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include a mechanism for Adam and the pedagogue or teacher to collaboratively identify and plan for specific times or lessons he finds difficult to manage.
